summary: Full four-file package and mandatory procedure reviewed. Existing selection rules already distinguish concrete contracts, compatible simpler alternatives, extension/lifecycle ownership and actual failure semantics. No confirmed technical or routing defect was found; no skill edits or version bump were made. Native synthetic controls corroborate a selection discriminator already present, not an improvement caused by this review.

requiredReadings: Root AGENTS.md; no applicable nested AGENTS.md found in assigned skill.
docs/skill-review-prompt.md (complete reading reused from prior wave-four assignment).
skills/skill-engineering/SKILL.md and evidence-and-confidence.md, evaluation.md, resource-design.md, anti-patterns.md (reread).
docs/skills-evolution-roadmap.md and prior wave-three results (relevant unchanged readings reused).
skills/gof-pattern-thinking/SKILL.md (read-only verification of required dependency and two-stage boundary).
procedure.parallelConstraints: No delegation, shared writes, global commands, installs, git-state mutations, neighboring edits or real-agent configuration changes.

promise.role: Second-stage mapping of known design forces into a shortlist, including no pattern; not implementation or broad architecture discovery.
activation: Which pattern fits a stated force
Explain an existing design through decisions
excluded: Restating the initial force-finding process owned by gof-pattern-thinking
Unrequested architecture redesign or tooling upgrades
successCriteria: Inspect caller, extension, configuration and lifecycle contracts when they determine the mapping.
Treat the matrix as candidate guidance rather than sufficient conditions or automatic rankings.
Preserve a viable language feature, direct loop, DI mechanism or framework hook.
Compare meaningful alternatives and state the cost or constraint deciding the recommendation.
Identify first-match, required-stage, state transition, policy and notification semantics rather than infer them from a name.
Keep compatibility, runtime/distributed guarantees and execution evidence distinct.
promise.javaContract: The skill conditions records/sealed types on Java 17 and finalized type-pattern switch on Java 21, with target inspection and no implied upgrades. Existing artifacts are prose/pseudocode, not executable application examples. New evidence-only fixtures compiled with --release 17 using Temurin 25.0.3+9 and ran on that Java 25 VM; Java 17 runtime execution was not performed.

adequate.evidence: Output allows no pattern, reuses settled forces, inspects callers and asks only discriminating questions; compatibility and simpler-implementation branches remain explicit.
adequate.consequence: No additional discovery interview or generic decision template is needed.

adequate.evidence: The chain row and adjacent guidance explicitly separate first-match candidates from required checks, including overlap, precedence, failure and empty/unhandled policy. Original GoF source and the retained Java controls support this distinction.
adequate.consequence: No new required-stage warning is justified: it is already taught where selection happens.

adequate.evidence: The current matrix distinguishes a subclass creation hook from a supplier and GoF representation assembly from fluent caller ergonomics; worked examples preserve public extension/failure/lifecycle contracts.
adequate.consequence: Do not collapse multiple creation roles or replace supported hooks merely because a simpler syntax exists.

adequate.evidence: Framework hooks are retained when coverage/order/lifecycle fit; Spring 6.2 proxy self-invocation exception is stated and source-confirmed.
adequate.consequence: Concern naming alone does not demand explicit decorators; no unconditional replacement rule found.

adequate.evidence: Graph edges are conditional candidates; visitor growth/fallback and Java target/ownership are explicitly considered. ElementVisitor17 confirms default-to-visitUnknown does not establish new-kind semantic support.
adequate.consequence: Preserve supported visitor extension contracts rather than mandating sealed-switch migration.

adequate.evidence: Undo/state composition does not imply external-effect reversal or durability; diagnosis distinguishes interface translation from races/authority/delivery.
adequate.consequence: No misleading automatic distributed guarantee was found.

consideredButNotAdded: Generic instructions to update every decision after feedback: current selection output, contract inspection and required reasoning dependency already cover the material behavior; no missing specialist decision established.
Extra implementation code or new reports: would change the selection role and add machinery without a supported defect.
New skill referrals inferred from pattern names: existing candidate labels are not automatically handoff instructions; declared referrals were checked without manufacturing dependencies.

Binary-evolution tutorial for exhaustive switch: the current ownership/extension/compatibility guards are adequate at selection level; JEP441 confirms separate compilation is an additional implementation consideration, not evidence that every switch recommendation here is wrong.

preserved: All four package files byte-for-byte, including metadata and dependency/suggestion contracts.
Discriminating questions, no-pattern decision branch, selection matrix and relationship graph.
Creation, structural and behavioral mappings with simpler alternatives.
Caller ergonomics, factory extension/lifecycle, framework interception and compositional role distinctions.
Capture mutability, type-set growth/fallbacks, undo/effect limits and distributed boundary handoffs.

parsedResult.limits: Local package validation and declared-target existence only; not catalog-wide version resolution or behavioral evaluation.

checks.limits: Strict metadata/adapter validation, two relative references, existence of 24 declared targets (one dependency plus 23 suggestions), four baseline hashes. Does not resolve all registry versions or validate global routing.

fullResult.limits: Native execution of synthetic contract controls, not an agent evaluation or a skill before/after comparison.

checks.interpretation: Compilation succeeded. first/any and all/all each passed 5/5 vectors. first/all and all/any each intentionally failed 3/5 vectors and exited 1. The wrapper verified expected exits and itself exited 0. The failures are deliberate negative controls, not failed package checks.
checks.oracle: Literal expected decisions and successful invocation traces for five vectors, including mixed answers, unanimous answers and no rules; failed requests may fail fast. The oracle is independent of the tested loops.
checks.limits: Synthetic single-thread local rules. This confirms the specific contract distinction already in the skill; not a performance test, Java 17 VM run, generated agent implementation or skill gain measurement.

behavioralEvidence.measuredSkillImprovement: Unavailable; no agent comparison and no revised skill.

walkthroughs.result: The supplied any contract and existing first-permitting loop fit. Keep the direct loop unless an additional extension force justifies linked handlers; a fixed set does not invalidate the conceptual chain role.

Only approval changes to all. A later denial must prevent eligibility, so first-permitting semantics are inadequate; direct required-stage iteration is enough, with explicit denial and empty-set behavior.

behavioralEvidence.decisiveConstraint: config/eligibility.json.approval = any versus all; every other actor input is identical.
behavioralEvidence.classification: Known development/regression pair informed by the existing selection-matrix rule, not held out.
behavioralEvidence.coordinatorProtocol: Give each isolated actor only one input JSON and ordinary skill resources. Materialize its files if tool-based inspection is desired. Withhold criteria, controls, sibling input and this handoff. Keep model/tools/settings comparable and capture actual outputs/resource access. No framework installation is needed; optional reproduction of native controls needs an available javac/java with --release 17 support.

sources.title: Design Patterns: Chain of Responsibility — GoF authors, publisher excerpt
sources.support: Requests pass through candidate receivers until handled and can remain unhandled; the name alone does not guarantee all-stage processing.
sources.limits: Original pattern account, not proof of any application framework or workflow. The all-required alternative is derived from the supplied business contract.

sources.title: ElementVisitor — Java SE 17 API
sources.support: Default methods for new constructs support source compatibility while delegating to unknown-kind behavior; concrete semantic support requires checking the visitor.
sources.limits: Does not establish every visitor design or source/binary evolution contract.

sources.title: JEP 441: Pattern Matching for switch
sources.support: Confirms finalized Java21 syntax and that compile-time exhaustiveness is not an unconditional runtime/evolution guarantee.
sources.limits: Feature design/contract evidence, not execution across Java releases. No switch implementation was introduced or executed in this review.

sources.title: Spring Framework 6.2: Proxying Mechanisms
sources.support: Direct calls through this bypass proxy advice; AspectJ weaving differs. Confirms the existing conditional framework-hook guidance.
sources.limits: No Spring integration test was run, and this does not describe every interceptor mechanism.

limitations: No supported defect found and no final content delta; no behavioral gain is claimed.
The package covers many decisions; four focused primary-source checks and synthetic controls do not prove every deployment or pattern composition.
No actor evaluation, external API/framework/database integration, performance benchmark or concurrency test was executed.
Technical fixtures compiled --release 17 on Temurin25.0.3+9; this is not Java17 runtime validation.
The case pair exercises an existing explicit teaching rule, so baseline/no-skill actors may already pass.
Existing validator dist was reused without rebuilding. Global registry/routing/version resolution and repository-wide verification are deferred.

Broad web search returned secondary material as well; only the four retained primary sources support the technical review. Truncated aggregate tool output was followed with focused reads for the assigned graph and reference sections.
